source: Beaty, Seli, Schacter (2019) Network neuroscience of creative cognition
finding: Narrative review. It reports no effect sizes. The DMN is tied to idea generation, the ECN to guiding and constraining it. Evidence is mostly correlational.
numbers: No pooled effect size. Table 1 lists 10 studies from 2017-2018 with n from 22+22 to 1,277.
limits: Authors say it is unclear whether connectivity is causal. No brain-stimulation study yet had changed DN-ECN interaction. Table has source inconsistencies (Liu et al. figural vs verbal; Chen 2016 vs 2018).
agent_relevance: The two-phase claim (loose generation, then control) rests on correlational data. Treat it as a design heuristic, not a proven mechanism.

source: Beaty, Seli, Schacter (2019) Network neuroscience of creative cognition - salience network claim
finding: The review makes no independent claim about the salience network. It appears only as part of the high-creative connectivity network and in an Openness state analysis.
numbers: No SN-specific numbers in the review.
limits: Salience as a switch between DMN and ECN is an inference, not a tested result in this review. The 2026 LLM review repeats the switch idea citing Beaty 2018 and Lloyd-Cox 2022.
agent_relevance: Do not build a salience-switch operator on neuroscience grounds. The switching rule must be justified on its own.

source: Beaty, Seli, Schacter (2019) Network neuroscience of creative cognition - Table 1 individual-difference studies
finding: Connectivity predicted creativity in several samples, but networks differed by measure and imaging mode.
numbers: Beaty 2018 n=163; Liu 2018 n=236 (rest fMRI + genetics, 2 datasets); Zhu 2017 n=282 (ECN mediated DN-creativity link); Sun 2018 n=574 (only DN within-network variability of 13 networks correlated); Kenett 2018 n=416 DTI (right DLPFC controllability); Chen 2018 n=159 (ECN gray-matter maturation predicted later creativity); Takeuchi 2017 n=1,277.
limits: Liu and Beaty networks overlapped only partly (figural vs verbal; rest vs task). Small groups: Gao 2017 and Li 2017 used 22 high vs 22 low creative.
agent_relevance: Neural signatures do not transfer cleanly across task type. Expect scaffold effects to be task-specific too.

source: Beaty, Seli, Schacter (2019) Network neuroscience of creative cognition - lesion evidence (Bendetowicz 2018, as summarised)
finding: Lesions in medial prefrontal cortex (DMN) impaired generating remote concepts. Lesions in rostrolateral PFC (ECN) impaired combining them but spared generation.
numbers: 29 patients, 54 controls (as reported in the review table).
limits: Seen only through the 2019 review, not read in full. Small patient sample.
agent_relevance: Gives a causal split: generate and combine are separable. Fits separate generation and control steps.

source: Beaty, Seli, Schacter (2019) Network neuroscience of creative cognition - sex difference (Takeuchi 2017, as summarised)
finding: Resting connectivity between left IFG and MPFC was positive in females and negative in males in relation to creativity.
numbers: n=1,277 (review table).
limits: Seen only through the review. Shows a moderator the creativity-network story mostly ignores.
agent_relevance: Individual-difference moderators exist; do not assume one fixed control setting fits all.

source: Beaty et al. (2018) Robust prediction of individual creative ability from brain functional connectivity (PNAS)
finding: Connectome-based predictive modelling: whole-brain task connectivity predicted divergent-thinking originality. The high-creative network held default, salience and executive hubs.
numbers: Internal n=163 (113 women). High-creative network 224 edges, r(161)=0.30, p=1.29e-4, permutation p=0.001. Low-creative network 603 edges, r=0.22, p=0.004. Of 35,778 possible edges (268 regions). Top 25 high-creative nodes: 12 default, 4 salience, 3 frontoparietal; hubs left PCC (k=19), left anterior insula (k=14), right DLPFC (k=8).
limits: Modest effects. Creativity score vs self-reported creative behaviour r(161)=0.54. Samples mostly women, art/music/science majors. Correlational.
agent_relevance: Default, salience and executive nodes together carry the signal, which supports a three-part design, but only modestly (r about 0.3).

source: Beaty et al. (2018) Robust prediction of individual creative ability from brain functional connectivity (PNAS) - external validation
finding: The high-creative network generalised to three independent datasets. The low-creative network mostly failed to validate.
numbers: External 1 (Austria, task, n=39): high r(37)=0.35 p=0.03; low r=-0.04. External 2 (n=54): high r(52)=0.28 p=0.03; low r=0.02. External 3 (China, rest, n=405): high r(403)=0.13 p=0.008; low r=0.11 p=0.03.
limits: Effect shrinks from r 0.30 to 0.13 in the resting-state sample. Authors say the low-creative network did not validate consistently, and one significant external result was in an unexpected direction.
agent_relevance: Expect real effects of this kind to be small (r 0.1 to 0.35). Do not expect large lifts from a brain-inspired scaffold.

source: Beaty et al. (2018) Robust prediction of individual creative ability from brain functional connectivity (PNAS) - control task and intelligence
finding: The model was specific to divergent thinking, not general ability.
numbers: Control object-characteristics task: high-network r(161)=0.05, p=0.47. External 2 control task high r=0.12, p=0.38. Fluid intelligence in resting sample: high r=0.04, p=0.39.
limits: Openness not examined. Fluid intelligence tested in one sample only. Underpowered to compare high vs low networks (Steiger z=0.83, p=0.40).
agent_relevance: Creative-generation skill is separable from general reasoning skill, so a scaffold for it may need its own tests.

source: Beaty et al. (2015) Default and executive network coupling supports creative idea production (Sci Rep)
finding: During an alternate-uses task versus an object-characteristics control, a network spanning default (PCC, precuneus, inferior parietal) and executive (DLPFC) regions was found. Seed and temporal analyses showed DLPFC-PCC-precuneus coupling at different task stages.
numbers: Final sample n=25 (13 female, mean age 21.04) after excluding 3 of 28 for head motion. Network affiliation confirmed in an independent resting-state sample.
limits: Small sample. Second-level connectivity contrasts at voxelwise p<.001 uncorrected. Correlational.
agent_relevance: Origin of the cooperating DMN and ECN claim. Small N; later work found smaller effects.

source: Beaty et al. (2014) Creativity and the default network: functional connectivity at rest (Neuropsychologia)
finding: High-creative people had stronger resting connectivity between left inferior frontal gyrus and the whole default network than low-creative people. Right IFG also coupled more with bilateral inferior parietal cortex and left DLPFC.
numbers: High-creative n=12 vs low-creative n=12, top and bottom 33% of a screened sample, matched on intelligence (p=.203), openness (p=.101), age (p=.287), gender.
limits: Tiny groups; extreme-group design inflates effects. Authors note causal claims are not supported.
agent_relevance: Cooperation between control regions and DMN, not DMN alone, marks creative ability. A weak base for strong design claims.

source: Cogdell-Brooke et al. (2020) Meta-analysis of fMRI studies of divergent thinking (ALE), Hum Brain Mapp
finding: Pooled fMRI of divergent thinking found four clusters: left inferior parietal lobe, left inferior frontal/precentral gyrus, superior/medial frontal gyrus, right cerebellum. The largest overlap was with the semantic control network, not the default network.
numbers: 20 studies met criteria; 162 foci in 19 experiments, 596 participants (divergent > control). Control > divergent: 35 foci in 8 experiments. Single-response vs multiple-response tasks: no significant difference.
limits: Only the AUT had enough studies for a task-specific analysis. ALE tests activation, not connectivity.
agent_relevance: Rival to the DMN-ECN story: semantic retrieval plus semantic control may explain creative generation. For an LLM, controlled retrieval fits better than free wandering.

source: Beaty et al. (2020) Default network contributions to episodic and semantic processing during divergent creative thinking (NeuroImage)
finding: Representational similarity analysis: DMN subregions are not purely episodic or purely semantic. Semantic-induction patterns matched idea generation in PCC, left angular gyrus and left anterior IPL. Episodic patterns matched in left parahippocampal and right IPL.
numbers: 28 adults, 23 in fMRI after 5 excluded. Semantic distance after semantic induction M=.84 (SD .04) vs after episodic induction M=.81 (SD .04), t(27)=3.11, p=.004. PCC t=3.34 p=.005; left AG t=2.59 p=.017; left parahippocampal t=2.79 p=.009. Recall 89.05% episodic vs 83.93% semantic, p=.04.
limits: One response per trial, so no fluency or flexibility. Small, mostly female sample. LSA scoring may favour the semantic effect. Authors call interpretations tentative.
agent_relevance: Priming with semantic associates raised originality; episodic priming helped other dimensions in earlier work. The retrieval cue is a lever for prompts.

source: Barnett and Vasiu (2026) Flow, DMN-ECN connectivity, creativity and emotion regulation (systematic review, Front Hum Neurosci)
finding: Nine neuroimaging studies of flow found core DMN down-regulation, more lateral prefrontal and parietal activity, and DMN-ECN connectivity between networks usually anti-correlated.
numbers: 9 studies met inclusion criteria; tasks from video games to jazz improvisation.
limits: Small, heterogeneous set; mixed modalities; no pooled effect. Only abstract and introduction read.
agent_relevance: Generation and control may run together, not strictly in two phases. Counter-evidence for a strict phase split.

source: Ovando-Tellez et al. (2025) Switching, fast and slow: memory search, brain connectivity and creativity (Imaging Neuroscience)
finding: Semantic search follows optimal-foraging (marginal value theorem) on the whole, but some responses deviate. Connectome prediction showed clustering responses were predicted by executive and attention networks, not memory-association networks, against the usual view.
numbers: Study 1 n=86 (43 women). Study 2 n=92 independent, 49 cue words vs 3. Pre-switch timing predicts fluency: R2=0.313, F(1,84)=39.66 (Study 1); R2=0.690, F(1,90)=214.3 (Study 2). CPM: fast-switching rs=.33 p=.002 (permutation p=.019); slow-clustering rs=.33 p=.002 (perm p=.024); fast-clustering rs=.23 p=.036 and slow-switching rs=-.18 p=.09 did not survive.
limits: Behavioural result replicated in an independent sample; the brain result was not. Switching was predicted by DMN-salience and DMN-visual links plus within-DMN links.
agent_relevance: Switching between idea clusters has its own signature and mixes default and control. Suggests a timed switch (leave a cluster when returns drop), not a fixed two-phase order.

source: Ovando-Tellez et al. (2025) - creativity policy differs from fluency policy
finding: The memory-search policy linked to creative performance differs from the policy that maximises fluency under the marginal value theorem.
numbers: Deviations from the marginal value prediction (slow clustering, fast switching) are the ones linked to brain connectivity and creative scores.
limits: Authors give this as an interpretation; the creative-score link comes through mediation in one MRI sample (n=86).
agent_relevance: More ideas per minute is not the same as more creative ideas. Do not optimise fluency alone in the agent.

source: Lloyd-Cox, Chen, Beaty (2022) The time course of creativity: multivariate classification of default and executive network contributions (Cortex)
finding: Studied how default and executive network contributions change over time in creative cognition. Cited by the 2026 LLM review as support for DMN generating and ECN evaluating.
numbers: Not read this session; numbers unavailable (publisher page returned 403).
limits: Not opened; no effect sizes.
agent_relevance: Only a lead for time-ordering of generation and control; verify before use.

source: Functional differentiation of the default and frontoparietal control networks predicts creative achievement (Cerebral Cortex, 2025)
finding: Creative achievement was linked to greater separation of control and default networks, a different emphasis from the coupling story. Most predictors did not replicate between samples.
numbers: Sample 1 n=236 (community, ages 20-40); Sample 2 n=234 (STEM, ages 16-38). Group gradients similar across samples (r=0.81 and 0.82). Sample 2 FPCN-A/DN-A b=1.99 P<.01 but b=0.22 adj P=0.11 without the intelligence covariate. Sample 1 arts: SVAN-A/FPCN-A b=-.63 P=.02. Gradient range: Sample 2 overall CAQ b=0.14 adj P=0.01; not replicated in Sample 1.
limits: Authors call the work preliminary. CAQ scoring differed across samples. Effects depend on the intelligence covariate. The segregation pattern appears in both samples but in different domains (arts vs sciences).
agent_relevance: A partial failed replication. Both coupling and separation are claimed; the schema should not hard-code either as the mechanism.

source: Functional differentiation (Cerebral Cortex, 2025) - Openness result
finding: Openness/Intellect was linked to temporoparietal gradient range in Sample 1 only.
numbers: Sample 1 beta=-.21 adj P=0.01 (Openness aspect beta=-.23 adj P=0.04; Intellect beta=-.06 P=0.68). Not replicated in Sample 2.
limits: Openness measured differently in the two samples. No association with overall range, dispersion or segregation after FDR correction.
agent_relevance: Personality moderator is fragile; do not condition agent behaviour on a trait proxy.

source: Rostral prefrontal mediolateral gradient predicts creativity in frontotemporal dementia (Brain, 2026)
finding: Lesion-style test of the two-process idea. Rostromedial PFC (DMN-linked) was critical for generating remote associates; rostrolateral PFC (ECN-linked) for combining them; both for overall creative ability. The range of the DMN-ECN gradient predicted creativity.
numbers: 45 participants (18 behavioural-variant FTD, 27 controls) for behaviour and VBM; gradient mapping in 24 controls, replicated in two independent young-adult datasets.
limits: Small patient group; atrophy is diffuse; cross-sectional. fMRI excluded 3 patients and 3 controls for motion.
agent_relevance: Best causal-style support for separate generate and combine steps. Supports a combine step distinct from the generate step.

source: Huang, Liu, Yang (2026) Evaluation of LLMs as tools, models and partners in creative thinking research (GCA framework)
finding: Selective narrative review, 2018 to June 2026. LLMs beat average humans on divergent-thinking tasks in most independent comparisons but not top humans. It states there is no evidence LLMs instantiate human-like creative mechanisms, and calls the DMN-generates / ECN-evaluates mapping onto LLMs heuristic, not exact.
numbers: Hedges g about 0.5 to 2.6 for LLM advantage. Hubert 2024 AUT originality g=2.61 [2.30,2.91] (post hoc fluency matching); Koivisto and Grassini 2023 AUT originality g=0.70 [0.33,1.06] (prospective fluency matching); Grassini and Koivisto 2025 flexibility g=0.74, subjective creativity g=-1.31 (humans better); Bellemare-Pepin 2026 DAT g=0.52 vs population average, g=-0.88 vs top half of humans. Automated scoring ICC >= 0.80, r >= 0.70 in selected studies.
limits: Not pre-registered; no pooled estimate; AUT items may be in training data, so upper bounds. Fluency control changes effect sizes a lot (2.61 vs 0.70).
agent_relevance: Direct statement that the brain analogy for LLM creativity is not validated. Use it as design inspiration only.

source: Bellemare-Pepin et al. (2026) Divergent creativity in humans and large language models (Sci Rep)
finding: Models were scored on the Divergent Association Task and on haiku, synopses and flash fiction against 100,000 humans. Some LLMs beat average humans on DAT but stay below the top half of humans.
numbers: 100,000 humans on DAT. 503 model responses vs 500 humans: g=0.52 over average, g=-0.88 against top half (as tabulated by the 2026 review). Prompt strategy changed scores: the etymology strategy beat the basic DAT prompt for GPT-3.5 and GPT-4; the meaning-opposition strategy lowered scores. Temperature raised semantic divergence for several models.
limits: Closed models' size and architecture unknown. Semantic distance measures associative divergence only, not usefulness.
agent_relevance: Prompt strategy and temperature are cheap levers on loose generation. The study tests generation only, with no control phase.

source: Bellemare-Pepin et al. (2026) - brainstorm then select reference
finding: The paper cites Summers-Stay et al. 2023 'Brainstorm, then Select': a two-phase prompt raised GPT-3.5 AUT scores, surpassing human scores in some instances.
numbers: Details of the primary study not read; only the claim as cited.
limits: Cited second-hand. Numbers missing.
agent_relevance: Closest LLM analogue of loose generation then control. Needs the primary paper before trusting the effect size.

source: Khalil et al. (2025) Adaptive decision-making fast and slow: a model of creative thinking (Eur J Neurosci)
finding: Proposes a framework of bottom-up and top-down systems with temporal modulation and individual differences, linking creativity to adaptive decision-making.
numbers: No empirical effect sizes; conceptual model.
limits: Framework paper; untested predictions. Only abstract and introduction read.
agent_relevance: Conceptual support for two modes with timing control; not evidence.

source: Ovando-Tellez et al. (2025) - replication status
finding: Behavioural foraging effects replicated across two samples; brain-behaviour CPM effects were found in one MRI sample only, and two of four components were lost after permutation tests.
numbers: Behavioural R2 0.313 and 0.690. CPM before permutation: 3 of 4 significant; after: 2 of 4 (p=.019, p=.024).
limits: Same lab and sample for MRI; no independent brain replication.
agent_relevance: Behavioural search dynamics are sturdier than their brain mapping. Borrow the behaviour, skip the anatomy.

source: Cross-study synthesis by this agent: coupling vs segregation tension
finding: Beaty 2014/2015/2018 report more DMN-ECN coupling in creative people; the 2025 achievement study reports more differentiation; Cogdell-Brooke 2020 points to semantic control. The differences follow measure (task vs rest, ability vs achievement, connectivity vs activation).
numbers: Prediction effects range r 0.13 to 0.35; extreme-group studies n=12 per group.
limits: Synthesis from opened papers, not a formal test.
agent_relevance: The field has not isolated one network mechanism. Judge any scaffold grounded in it by its own benchmark gain.
